name: Ukrainian
variety: Standard Ukrainian (literary norm based on the central Dnieper dialects, as spoken in Kyiv)
sources: Pompino-Marschall, Bernd; Steriopolo, Elena & Żygis, Marzena (2017). Ukrainian. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 47(3), 349-357.
Shevelov, George Y. (1993). Ukrainian. In B. Comrie & G. G. Corbett (eds.), The Slavonic Languages. London: Routledge.
Shevelov, George Y. (1979). A Historical Phonology of the Ukrainian Language. Heidelberg: Carl Winter.
Zilynskyj, Ivan (1979). A Phonetic Description of the Ukrainian Language. Cambridge, MA: Harvard Ukrainian Research Institute.
Danyenko, Andrii & Vakulenko, Serhii (1995). Ukrainian. München: Lincom Europa.
Pugh, Stefan M. & Press, Ian (1999). Ukrainian: A Comprehensive Grammar. London: Routledge.
Buk, Solomija; Mačutek, Ján & Rovenchak, Andrij (2008). Some properties of the Ukrainian writing system. Glottometrics 16.
contrasts: palatalised versus plain consonants in the dental and alveolar series only (/t d s z t͡s d͡z n l r/); labials, velars and postalveolars have no soft phonemes, only slightly palatalised allophones before /i/
voiced glottal fricative /ɦ/ versus velar stop /ɡ/ (rare) versus voiceless /x/
long (geminate) consonants, mostly soft dentals between vowels (життя [ʒɪˈtʲːɑ], знання [znɑˈnʲːɑ])
voiced versus voiceless obstruents, kept word-finally (дуб [dub])
position of stress is lexically contrastive (замок: [ˈzɑmɔk] 'castle' vs [zɑˈmɔk] 'lock')
allophony: /ʋ/ is [ʋ] before front vowels, [w] before back rounded vowels, and the glide [u̯] after a vowel before a consonant or word-finally (вовк [wɔu̯k], правда [ˈprɑu̯dɑ], любов [lʲuˈbɔu̯]); word-initially before a consonant it is [u̯] or [w] (вчора); it is not devoiced to [f]

voiceless obstruents are voiced before voiced obstruents (боротьба [bɔrɔdʲˈbɑ], просьба [ˈprɔzʲbɑ], вокзал [wɔɡˈzɑl]); voiced obstruents stay voiced before voiceless ones (казка [ˈkɑzkɑ], дужка), except /ɦ/ to [x] in легко, вогко, нігті, кігті and the prefix з- before voiceless consonants

unstressed /ɛ/ and /ɪ/ approach each other ([e̞] and [ɪ̞]); unstressed /ɔ/ is raised to [o] before a syllable with /u/ or /i/ (кожух, зозуля); unstressed /ɑ/ is slightly centralised; there is no akanye
labials, velars and postalveolars are slightly palatalised before /i/ (білий, хід, шість)
/rʲ/ occurs only before vowels; syllable-final /r/ is hard
/l/ is dental and moderately velarised; /r/ is an alveolar trill or tap; /ɦ/ is voiced
phonotactics: preference for open syllables, supported by the alternations у/в and і/й according to the neighbouring sounds
hard consonants only before /ɪ/ and /ɛ/ in native words; only soft (or slightly palatalised) consonants before /i/
geminates arise from consonant plus /j/ (життя, зілля) and at morpheme boundaries (віддати)
the apostrophe marks a hard consonant followed by [j] (м'ясо [ˈmjɑsɔ], п'ять)

stress.rule: Stress can fall on any syllable and may shift within a paradigm; it is not shown in ordinary spelling.
stress.cues: duration and intensity; vowel quality changes little; weaker contrast between stressed and unstressed syllables than in Russian

rhythm.vowel_reduction: weak: unstressed vowels keep their identity, with partial merging of /ɛ/ and /ɪ/ and raising of /ɔ/ before high vowels
rhythm.notes: Secondary stresses are common in longer words.

length.notes: No phonemic vowel length. Geminate consonants are contrastive, mostly long soft dentals between vowels and geminates at morpheme boundaries; no duration ratio is quoted here.

intonation.declarative: rising or high accents on non-final stressed syllables, final fall to low on the nuclear stressed syllable
intonation.yes_no_question: rise on the stressed syllable of the word in focus followed by a fall on the post-tonic syllables; the particle чи may introduce the question
intonation.wh_question: high accent on the question word, then a gradual fall to low
intonation.continuation: rise on the last stressed syllable of the non-final phrase
intonation.accent_shape: rising accents before the nucleus; falling nuclear accent in statements
intonation.notes: Described on the basis of the reference grammars; detailed instrumental studies are few.

tone.notes: No lexical tone or pitch accent.

problems: Stress: there is no stress dictionary (uk_list has about 225 lines, mostly symbols and numbers) and the position is guessed from the number of syllables by the routine written for Russian, so many common words are wrong: вода, село, весна get initial stress, молоко and голова get stress on the second syllable (all have final stress).
в is always a bilabial fricative [β] (phoneme B) and is devoiced to [f] before voiceless consonants (вовк [βofk], вчора [ftʃora]); the glide [u̯] after vowels and initial [w] are missing.

The Russian setting for regressive voicing is used, so voiced obstruents are devoiced before voiceless ones (казка [kaska]), which standard Ukrainian does not do; легко keeps [h] instead of [x]; voicing before a voiced obstruent fails across a soft sign (боротьба [borotba], просьба [prosba]).

Palatalisation exists only for л and н (as palatal [ʎ ɲ]) and for сь, ць before vowels: д, т, з, с before і stay hard (діти, тінь, сіль), я ю є after д т з с ц р are read as [j] plus vowel (дякую [djakuju], рясно [rjasno], щастя [ʃtʃastja]) and final ть is hard (п'ять [pjat]).
Long soft consonants are read as hard geminate plus [j] (життя [ʒɪttja]).
і and ї are always long [iː]; Ukrainian has no vowel length.
г is the voiceless [h], not voiced [ɦ].
No raising of unstressed о before high vowels and no partial merger of unstressed е and и (minor).
Only the default eSpeak tunes are used; wh-questions get the same fall-rise as yes-no questions.
good: no final devoicing (дуб, сад, хліб keep voiced consonants)
apostrophe handled (м'ясо, пір'я), щ as [ʃt͡ʃ], дз and дж as affricates

notes: No formant, VOT or rhythm-metric values are given because I cannot quote published figures with confidence.
